x: The first race was the 100 yds., Bowers running very well to be beaten by inches, Ransome, T.C.C., winning in 10-9, Botwright 3rd. Ransome also scored in the 220 yds., Botwright finishing 2nd and Bowers 4th.
Unfortunately we were unable to turn out a very strong team, but the home team were given quite a good match. Bowers and Bennett finished 2nd and 5th in both 100 yds. and 220 yds.

The match against Southgate, at Broomfield Park, took place in glorious weather, and some keen racing was seen, as the result below will show, the club winning with 58 points to 51 points. 100 Yards.—(1) Marin (S); (2) Bowers (B); (5) Bennett (B). 10.5. 880 Yards.—(1) Marchant (B); (2) Orton (B). 2mins. 5.4.
Webb (B); (4) Stimpson (B). 55.2. 100 Yards.—(1) Bowers (B); Pritchard (B). 10.6. 100 Yards Junior.—(1) Patterson (T.V.); (2) Nunn (B); (3) Bateman (B). 10.7.

100 Yards Junior.—(1) White (O.M.W.); (2) H.H.M.; (3) Bateman (B). 11.2. 100 Yards Senior.—(1) Russell (W.G.); (2) Bowers (B); Green (S); Pritchard (B). 10.8. 220 Yards Junior.—(1) Hayes (H.H.M.); (2) Bateman (B); (3) O.M.W. 25.3. 220 Yards Senior.—(1) Green (S); (2) Read (B); (3) Jarlett (B). 24.3.…
In the 100 yards, Bowers and F.
Bowers gained a double, winning the 100 yards and 220 yards, with Frank Simmons 4th. The 440 yards was an easy win for Frank Webb, with Tommy Morrell, taking up sprinting, 2nd.

The return match with the Police was marked by the appearance of so many middle distance men; no fewer than seven Belgrave men ran in the mile, which was won by Arthur Cooper, T.V.H., running for Belgrave. Bowers again ran very well, taking both the 100 yards and 220 yards.
Elliott, of the T.C.C., made up ground on Bowers and a bad take-over between the latter and Hayes saw Holmes send off the T.C.C. man in the lead for the final quarter.
Bowers, of our own club, also showed improved form to gain second place in the 100 yards, but our other runner in the 220, A.

There were no field events, it being a purely track meeting, and they had first and second string races with the 1 Mile and 3 Miles being run on the team principle. In the 100 Yards, Bill Bowers was third, with M.
Broadbent, the young Wallington schoolboy, in the sprints. In the 100 Yards, Bill Bowers ran extremely well, to be narrowly beaten by A.
Bowers third. Wigley repeated his win in the 220, but this time Bowers moved up a place, with Metcalfe of the Poly. taking second place.
Bowers, on leave from the Navy, running third in both races.
